title: Flying Officer A D S Snell
inscription: IN LOVING AND EVERLASTING/ REMEMBRANCE OF/ F/O. A. DENNIS SERPELL SNELL/ AGED 21./ BOMBER COMMAND./ MISSING FROM OPERATIONS OVER ITALY/ JULY 14TH/15TH 1943. BELOVED SON OF/ ARTHUR AND FRANCES MARY SNELL/ AT THE GOING DOWN OF THE SUN/ AND IN THE MORNING, WE WILL REMEMBER HIM

title: Flying Officer L T Manser VC
inscription: IN MEMORY OF/FLYING OFFICER/LESLIE THOMAS MANSER, V.C./50TH SQUADRON R.A.F./KILLED IN ACTION ON THE 31ST MAY 1942/DURING THE FIRST/THOUSAND BOMBER RAID ON COLOGNE/AGED 20 YEARS./"HE PRESSED ON TO HIS TARGET OVERCOMING GREAT ENEMY/OPPOSITION AND GAVE HIS LIFE TO SAVE HIS CREW."/

title: Flying Officer P Pease
inscription: Flying Officer A. Peter Pease / Royal Air Force Volunteer Reserve // (image) / Eldest son of Sir Richard and Lady Pease / Born in London 15 February 1918 / Raised in Richmond, Yorkshire / Educated at Eton College and Trinity College, Cambridge / On 15 September 1940, all England stood on alert / Many expected the German invasion would come any day / Shortly after three in the afternoon / A large formation of German bombers / Was attacked in the skies above this spot / By the Spitfires of 603 Squadron // While pressing his attack Peter Pease was struck / By cannon fire of an enemy fighter / He fell in flames in the field southeast of this spot / His last act was to rev his engine to avoid nearby houses / A tree now stands where he fell // (image) / Doubt not that in this lonely field was laid / A heart once pregnant with celestial fire; / Hands that the rod of empire might have swayed, ‘ Or waked to ecstasy the living lyre. // In loving memory / Some of the many / Honour this one of the few / 15 September 2015 / Battle of Britain Day

title: Flying Officer R McG Waterston
inscription: IN MEMORY OF/ FLYING OFFICER/ ROBIN McGREGOR/ "BUBBLE" WATERSTON/ OF NO. 630 SQUADRON AUX A.F./ WHO LOST HIS LIFE/ NEAR THIS SPOT/ ON 31st AUGUST 1940/ IN SPITFIRE X4273/ HE WAS 23 YEARS OLD/ ONE OF CHURCHILL'S FEW/ MEMORIAL DEDICATED ON/ 29th SEPT. 2009/ BY THE/ SHOREHAM AIRCRAFT MUSEUM/ KENT.

title: Pilot Officer H R Case
inscription: THE CASE MEMORIAL PANELS // The display panels you see around the Memorial site are / dedicated to the memory of Pilot Officer Herbert Robert Case. / He lost his life in the final stages of the battle of Britain / on 12 October 1940, when his Spitfire crashed in a field / not far from this site, after combat with enemy aircraft. // ONE OF THE FEW // Herbert Case, from Withycombe, Somerset, / had joined the RAF Volunteer Reserve in 1936 / and was called up immediately at the outbreak of war. / He served with Nos 64 and 72 Squadrons in 1940. / He was known as bright, cheerful and interested / in all things mechanical. A colleague remembered / him as a ‘young man keen to get to grips with the enemy’. // His early death at the age of 24 here at Capel-le-Ferne / symbolises the terrible but magnificent sacrifice made / by so many during the Battle of Britain. The names of the / nearly 33,000 aircrew who served, known as ‘The Few’, are recorded / at this site on the Christopher Foxley- Norris Memorial Wall. // Picture Caption – A pilot of / No. 64 Squadron, / in which / Herbert Case served, / scrambles to his / Spitfire. August, 1940. //

title: Sergeant R Bolitho
inscription: TO/ COMMEMORATE/ 50TH/ ANNIVERSARY/ 617 SQUADRON DAM BUSTERS/ SGT. RICHARD BOLITHO/ 1211045/ OF JAMES STREET KIMBERLEY/ REAR GUNNER AIRCRAFT ED 864 B-BAKER/ KILLED IN ACTION OPERATION CHASTISE/ DAMS RAID/ CRASHED ACHLING AARBEN. NTH DORSTEN/ 12:15 17TH MAY 1943

title: Flight Sergeant J Hannah VC - Rose Garden
inscription: THE HANNAH ROSE / IN MEMORY OF / F/SGT. JOHN HANNAH, V. C. / NO. 83 SQUADRON / ROYAL AIR FORCE SCAMPTON / RAISED BY F.W. SHAW OF WILLOUGHTON, THIS HYBRID ROSE IS THE COLOUR OF A VICTORIA CROSS RIBBON. / IT WAS PRESENTED TO NO. 83 SQUADRON IN HONOUR OF / JOHN HANNAH, WHO WON HIS V.C. BY BEATING OUT FIRE IN HIS / HAMPDEN AIRCRAFT, MAKING IT POSSIBLE TO RETURN TO THIS BASE / ON THE NIGHT OF SEPTEMBER 15th 1940. 2nd Plaque This rose garden is dedicated/ to the memory of/ Flight Sergeant John Hannah VC/ Wireless Operator and Air Gunner/ 27 Nov 1921 - 7 Jun 1947
